title: Institutional vs ad-hoc arbitration - what clients should actually choose
p1:
Many businesses choose arbitration thinking it automatically means faster and cheaper dispute resolution.

But the biggest decision is often ignored: should you choose institutional arbitration or ad-hoc arbitration?
p2:
A common misconception is that ad-hoc arbitration gives more control because parties manage everything themselves.

The reality? That flexibility can become a challenge when parties disagree on arbitrator appointments, timelines, procedures, or costs.
p3:
Institutional arbitration involves an established body that provides rules, administrative support, and a framework to keep the process moving. Ad-hoc arbitration allows parties to design the process themselves but requires greater cooperation.

For complex commercial disputes, institutional support can reduce uncertainty. For smaller disputes with trusted parties, ad-hoc arbitration may offer simplicity and lower administrative costs.

The right choice depends on the dispute, relationship between parties, and level of procedural certainty required.
conclusion: When drafting arbitration clauses, would you prefer the structure of institutional arbitration or the flexibility of ad-hoc arbitration?
